subject: Re: Request — Ephemeral transit assertions & rotation sample for Acme Payments
messages:
From: Lucia Perez <lucia.perez@acme-payments.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Feb 2029 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request — ephemeral transit assertions + rotation sample

Hi Olga,

We're working through a SIG + SOC 2 follow-up and need a compact set of artifacts that show how Redwood handles ephemeral KEKs in transit and a sample of key rotation telemetry. Specifically can you provide: 

- A short transit wrap/unwrap trace for an ephemeral KEK exchange (Jan 2029 sample) that shows envelope wrapping steps and the associated wrap/unwrap call IDs.
- HSM seal attestation for the same window (operator shift id + attestation pdf).
- Rotation log extract (first week of Jan 2029) with the rotation event IDs and operator IDs (redact tenant IDs if necessary).
- Keystore index snapshot (machine-readable) to show key lineage for the ephemeral keys.

We don't need full raw logs — a curated sampling and a manifest describing redaction is fine. Can you deliver this as a secure Drive link or SFTP by EOD 15 Feb? If there are any export quirks we should know about (formatting, gzip, column mapping), include them in a short README.

Thanks,
Lucia Perez
Head of Security, Acme Payments
lucia.perez@acme-payments.com
+1 (415) 555-0186

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Lucia Perez <lucia.perez@acme-payments.com>
Cc: alcyon-security@acme-payments.com
Date: Wed, 14 Feb 2029 09:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request — ephemeral transit assertions + rotation sample

Hi Lucia — thanks for the clear ask. We can provide a curated package that matches what you describe. High-level plan: 

1) Rotation log extract (CSV) with rotation event IDs, operator shift hashes, and timestamps. Tenant identifiers will be hashed (sha256) and mapped in a separate manifest so you can correlate without revealing PII.
2) Transit wrap trace (trimmed) containing the wrap/unwrap callflow and call IDs. Sensitive session tokens are redacted.
3) HSM seal attestation (scanned PDF) and a short operator shift manifest listing the operator alias and shift window.
4) Keystore index snapshot in JSONL (line-delimited) showing the ephemeral key lineage and parent KEK references.

We'll deliver via a secured, access-controlled Drive link and provide a README with column mappings and redaction notes. Target delivery: EOD 2029-02-15 (ETA ~24–36 hours). If that timeline works I'll mobilize the infra + compliance team.

One clarification: do you need operator identities replaced with full legal names or are hashed operator aliases acceptable for your audit?

Best,
Olga Petrov
Security & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
olga.petrov@redwood.com
(650) 555-0123

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Feb 2029 09:15:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Request — ephemeral transit assertions + rotation sample

Marissa / Jordan — forwarding Acme's request below. Can you assemble the artifacts and confirm the exact filenames and delivery method? Notes:

- Marissa: please generate the rotation_log_sample_20290101.csv and keystore_index_snapshot.jsonl. Include a one-paragraph README describing redaction (we hash tenant IDs, keep operator aliases as hashed values, and remove any IPs).
- Jordan: please extract the transit_wrap_trace_20290101.txt from the runtime tracing system and coordinate with infra to get the HSM seal PDF (hsm_seal_attestation_20290101.pdf). We need the HSM M-of-N seal ID and the attestation timestamp in the manifest.

Deliver to a secured Drive folder and tag it "acme/transit-assertions-2029-01". Aim to have a draft link for me by EOD tomorrow so I can review before we hand to Acme.

Thanks — Olga

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Feb 2029 12:02:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Request — ephemeral transit assertions + rotation sample

Olga — we've prepared a curated package and placed it into a restricted Drive folder. Delivery notes: 

Drive link (restricted): https://drive.redwood.com/secure/acme/transit-assertions-2029-01 (Access granted to lucia.perez@acme-payments.com)

Files included (manifest):
- rotation_log_sample_20290101.csv (3,242 rows trimmed to rotation events; tenant_id hashed with sha256; columns: event_id, timestamp_utc, operator_alias_hash, rotation_type, parent_kek_id)
- transit_wrap_trace_20290101.txt (trimmed callflow, includes wrap_call_id, unwrap_call_id, duration_ms; redacted ephemeral session tokens)
- hsm_seal_attestation_20290101.pdf (HSM vendor attestation signed; includes seal ID: SEA-7b9c; operator shift window: 2029-01-03T22:00Z - 2029-01-04T06:00Z)
- keystore_index_snapshot.jsonl (line-delimited entries showing key_id -> parent_kek_id -> creation_ts)
- README_acme_transit_202901.txt (redaction, column map, generation commands used)

Technical notes:
- The transit_wrap_trace was produced by sampling the runtime tracer and correlating call IDs with our wrap/unwrap service. We replaced full session tokens with token fingerprints (first 8 hex chars) and kept call IDs intact for traceability.
- The HSM attestation is an exported, vendor-signed PDF. We omitted full operator legal names and instead included operator_alias_hash for audit correlation. If Acme requires un-hashed operator names under an NDA, we can discuss a limited-scope disclosure process.

Attaching a short manifest and README in the folder. Let me know if I should create a one-page executive summary for the auditor.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Manager, Infrastructure Compliance
Redwood Inference

From: Lucia Perez <lucia.perez@acme-payments.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
Cc: alcyon-security@acme-payments.com
Date: Wed, 14 Feb 2029 15:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Request — ephemeral transit assertions + rotation sample

Olga / Marissa — received, thank you. I reviewed the manifest and the README; the redaction approach is acceptable for our SIG reviewers. A couple of follow-ups: 

1) Can you confirm the HSM seal ID (SEA-7b9c) is reproducible in the attestation chain? We will reference that seal ID in our audit notes.
2) For traceability we prefer operator alias hashes mapped to a short operator id (e.g., OP-001) in the manifest rather than full hashes only — can you add a small mapping file that shows operator_alias_hash -> OP-00X (no PII)?

If you can drop a tiny mapping file (operator_mapping_202901.csv) in the same Drive folder and confirm the HSM seal linkage, we can close this request on our side. Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Lucia
Head of Security, Acme Payments

Attachments referenced in message: rotation_log_sample_20290101.csv (CSV stub), hsm_seal_attestation_20290101.pdf (PDF stub), transit_wrap_trace_20290101.txt (TXT stub), keystore_index_snapshot.jsonl (JSONL stub)
